sources.README.md:
# Hotel incident worksheet


The workspace API drives a document editor and its save badge. The workspace store
holds draft text across navigation and closed editor views. Returning to a document
restores the user's last edit. Save integrations receive committed records and may
select another document synchronously. Later navigation means the navigation request that starts later takes precedence, even if an earlier request returns afterward. For example, if open(B) starts and saving the departed A invokes a callback that calls open(C), C remains selected after the callback and the outer open(B) return. If that callback calls close() instead, the editor remains closed after the outer open(B) returns. These are navigation results, independent of when the departed document's save occurs.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is available
through the store, even if the next view selects a different document.

`createSearchPreview` is an adjacent transient search panel. It publishes after a
40 ms quiet interval; hiding it discards an unpublished query. It can be reused.

The public methods are synchronous. Output render functions observe state; navigation
comes through the workspace API, including its `onSaved` integration. `store` provides
`read`, `write` and `subscribe`; `timers` provides `schedule(callback, delay)` and
`cancel(handle)`. Production timers use the browser's timers. Keep these interfaces.

sources.docs/host-api.md:
# Host integration

open(id), edit(text), close() and dispose() are synchronous entry points.
The store owns persisted document records independently of any mounted view.
Store delivery writes first, snapshots subscriptions, and skips removed listeners.
onSaved is called inline and can navigate or edit; rendering is an output sink.
Every open creates a fresh visit and subscription, including same-key reopen.
Injected timers provide schedule(callback,delay) and cancel(handle).
The preview is transient and independent of the editor's persistence policy.

<?php
class Store {
    private $records, $listeners = [], $serial = 0, $revision = 0;
    function __construct($records) { $this->records = $records; }
    function read($id) { return $this->records[$id] ?? ''; }
    function subscribe($fn) { $token = ++$this->serial; $this->listeners[$token] = $fn; return $token; }
    function stop($token) { unset($this->listeners[$token]); }
    function write($id, $text) {
        $this->records[$id] = $text;
        $event = ['id'=>$id, 'text'=>$text, 'revision'=>++$this->revision];
        foreach ($this->listeners as $token=>$fn) if (isset($this->listeners[$token])) $fn($event);
        return $event;
    }
}
class Trailing {
    private $env, $delay, $work, $handle = null, $pending = null;
    function __construct($env, $delay, $work) { $this->env=$env; $this->delay=$delay; $this->work=$work; }
    function push($value) {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $this->pending=$value;
        $this->handle=$this->env->schedule(function() { $this->flush(); }, $this->delay);
    }
    function flush() {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $value=$this->pending; $this->pending=null; $this->handle=null;
        if ($value !== null) ($this->work)($value);
    }
    function cancel() {
        if ($this->handle !== null) $this->env->cancel($this->handle);
        $this->pending=null; $this->handle=null;
    }
}

class Visit {
    private $env, $id, $stop, $task;
    function __construct($env, $id) {
        $this->env=$env; $this->id=$id;
        $token=$env->store->subscribe(function($e) use ($env, $id) { if ($e['id']===$id) $env->output('status',$e); });
        $this->stop=function() use ($env, $token) { $env->store->stop($token); };
        $this->task=new Trailing($env,120,function($text) use ($env,$id) { $env->write($id,$text); });
    }
    function accept($text) { $this->env->write($this->id,$text); }
    function depart() { ($this->stop)();$this->env->output('document',null); }
}
class Workspace {
    private $env, $current=null, $generation=0;
    function __construct($env) { $this->env=$env; }
    private function retire() { $old=$this->current; $this->current=null; if ($old) $old->depart(); else $this->env->output('document',null); }
    function open($id) { $ticket=++$this->generation; $this->retire(); if ($ticket!==$this->generation) return; $this->current=new Visit($this->env,$id); $this->env->output('document',['id'=>$id,'text'=>$this->env->store->read($id)]); }
    function edit($text) { $selected=$this->current; if ($selected) $selected->accept($text); }
    function close() { ++$this->generation; $this->retire(); }
    function dispose() { $this->close(); }
}
class Preview {
    private $task;
    function __construct($env) { $this->task=new Trailing($env,40,function($q) use ($env) { $env->output('preview',['query'=>$q]); }); }
    function query($text) { $this->task->push($text); }
    function hide() { $this->task->cancel(); }
}

Coalesce edits using the existing trailing utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save. Preserve other behavior and public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

limitations: This guidance assumes synchronous entry points and inline save callbacks; it does not establish behavior for asynchronous navigation or store delivery.
The public sources do not specify exception handling for store writes, timer operations, output sinks, or integration callbacks.
The concrete environment write implementation and committed-record shape are outside the supplied public sources.
A successful attempt plus a syntax check does not prove the guidance generalizes to other timer, callback, or ownership models.

rules.body: Apply this pattern when edits owned by a document visit must use trailing coalescing during the visit, while synchronous open, close, or dispose boundaries must make the latest accepted edit durable before returning.

Give each visit its own trailing task, bound to that visit's document identity, and push every accepted edit into it with the required quiet interval; replacing a pending edit must cancel the prior timer so only the latest value in the burst is committed.
A completed trailing flush must clear its handle and pending value so a later burst in the same visit can schedule and complete another save.

Before retiring a visit, remove its subscription and detach it from the workspace; then synchronously flush its pending trailing value so the departed document is durable and no retired timer or observer remains active.

Guard an outer navigation with a monotonically increasing generation or equivalent precedence token. Because an inline save callback may call open or close during retirement, the outer operation must check its token after retirement and must not render or select its original target if a later navigation has started.
Every open, including a same-key reopen, must allocate a fresh visit, subscription, and visit-owned trailing task; never reuse the retired visit merely because the document key matches.
Preserve synchronous public methods, store delivery semantics, output-only rendering, and committed-record callbacks; the persistence change must not redesign the injected store or timer interfaces.

Do not apply the editor's retirement-flush policy to an adjacent transient preview whose documented boundary policy discards unpublished work; preserve its independent 40 ms trailing delay, hide cancellation, and reusability.
Verify no write occurs before 120 ms of quiet, one write uses the latest text in a burst, and a later burst saves independently.

Verify open, close, and dispose synchronously persist the departed visit's latest accepted edit, including cases where the inline save callback starts a later open or close that must retain precedence.
Verify same-key reopening creates a fresh subscription and task, retired callbacks cannot write again, and the independent preview behavior remains unchanged.

Exercise an inline onSaved callback that calls close() while an outer open(B) is retiring A; the editor must remain closed.
Reopen the same document key and verify a fresh visit and subscription are created.
Run the public PHP syntax check after any Action.
Confirm Preview still publishes after 40 ms of quiet, hide() discards an unpublished query, and the preview remains reusable.
